title: Beyond the 956: Steve Camp, pioneering Christian music singer, dies at 71

content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Steve Camp, the contemporary Christian music singer, songwriter and pastor whose career in music and ministry spanned five decades, has died at 71.

Camp died on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, after a battle with heart failure, his family said in a statement. He was 71.

Born April 13, 1955, in Wheaton, Illinois, Camp released his first album, Sayin It with Love, in 1978 and signed with Sparrow Records. Over a career that began in 1975, he recorded 22 albums and scored 15 No. 1 songs, earning a Grammy nomination for his song “Love’s Not a Feeling,” featuring Michele Pillar.

Camp was a two-time cover artist for CCM Magazine and became known for his 1998 “107 Theses,” a call for reform in the contemporary Christian music industry. In later years he served as senior pastor of Crosslife Church in Fort Pierce, Florida.

Sources: Camp family statement; CCM Magazine; The Christian Post; Gospel Music Association.
